_why: It lives in JSON rather than in the gate script for one concrete reason: the
gate scans scripts/ INCLUDING ITSELF, so a network token written literally in
the gate would make the gate flag the gate. Keeping the tokens in data also
means adding a permitted module is a reviewable one-line diff and not an edit
network_globals are matched as source substrings, deliberately crudely — the
point is that a positive permit list cannot be defeated by a construct nobody
thought to name, so over-matching here costs a false alarm, never a miss.
_site_policy_why: RULING MADE AT P1, FLAGGED FOR RATIFICATION (see the P1 receipt).
The egress rule protects OUR CRAWLER's conduct toward third parties: our UA,
our schedule, our runner. Two kinds of code live under site/ and only one of
- Astro FRONTMATTER and every .ts/.mjs under site/ run at BUILD TIME on our
runner. A request from there IS our crawler, wearing no UA discipline and
bypassing pipeline/fetch/client.ts entirely. FORBIDDEN, no exceptions.
- A client <script> block runs in a VISITOR'S browser. That is a different
actor with a different posture, and forbidding it would also forbid
MapLibre loading tiles - a component plan section 2.5 mandates. Network
globals are permitted there; imports are still allowlisted.
The narrow version keeps the protection that matters: a build-time scrape
smuggled into site/ still fails this gate, and fixtures/site-frontmatter-egress.astro
